title: Normalize late-arriving telemetry for per-customer/model console heatmaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Rediscover and implement a stable normalization layer for late-arriving/retrofitted telemetry so that per-customer and per-model heatmaps in the Redwood Console do not show transient spikes or dips after backfills. Root cause: multiple ingestion pipelines (streaming shard ingest + batched backfill) apply different attribution heuristics, shard clocks sometimes reorder events at minute boundaries, and the current charting layer naively doubles-counts late events that overlap prior aggregate windows. Impact: customers see misleading per-model cost spikes and quota usages; on-call incidents (2026-03-02) and two support tickets escalated to SE showed incorrect billing guidance. Goal: provide deterministic, idempotent normalization that preserves time-window invariants, surfaces corrected deltas in the UI, and allows safe rollback of backfill corrections.
steps: Instrument a canonical event fingerprint (request_id + model_alias + ingest_shard + event_type) to detect duplicates across streaming and backfill paths
Add ingest-time canonicalization service that assigns a stable canonical_event_ts based on original event timestamp with shard-offset correction
Implement window-aware de-duplication during aggregation: prefer earliest canonical_event_ts within a window and drop duplicate token counts from backfilled batches if already counted

Add a reconciliation pipeline that emits 'correction' events instead of overwriting historical aggregates; update console charts to render correction overlays (positive/negative) and a toggle to show pre/post-correction series
Run a dry-backfill on a staging copy of production day X, compare results with current production aggregation, and validate with existing per-model billing test harness
Deploy canonicalization and de-duplication behind a feature flag; run shadow mode for 48h, evaluate variance metrics; if within thresholds, enable correction-event emission and UI toggle rollout
acceptance_criteria: Per-model daily delta after applying canonicalization <= 0.5% for non-sampled customers compared to validated ground-truth ledger
No customer-facing spike > 20% introduced by backfill windows after normalization
Console exposes a clear correction overlay with changelog link for any day that received backfill corrections
Automated test suite includes synthetic time-travel scenarios covering shard-clock skew and duplicate backfill events
Documented runbook for on-call to explain correction events and a rollback plan
comments: 2026-03-08 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Filed after postmortem for 2026-03-02 incident. Initial hypothesis: late backfill batches are counted in addition to streaming events because they carry different ingest_shard ids and no canonical fingerprint exists.

2026-03-09 11:03 - Marcus Li: Added proposed approach to emit correction events instead of in-place mutates. Prefer additive correction model to preserve auditability. Sketch: corrections are separate stream with {target_window, delta_tokens, reason}.

2026-03-10 16:40 - Emma García (Product): UI requirement: show corrections as a translucent overlay on heatmaps and include a tooltip that links to a reconciliation detail page. PM OKs staged rollout.

2026-03-11 08:55 - Marcus Li: Prototype of canonical_event_fingerprint implemented in infra repo. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821 (draft). Needs integration tests for cross-shard duplicates.

2026-03-12 14:27 - SRE Team: Observability note — shard-clock-skew metric (shard_clock_offset_seconds) spikes on 2026-03-02. We should add guard rails rejecting events with offset > 300s unless backfill flag is set.

2026-03-13 10:00 - QA: Created synthetic fixtures simulating backfills arriving 2hr late and same-minute reorderings. Current aggregation shows double-count of 3-7% under baseline; expected to reduce to <0.5% after de-duplication.

2026-03-14 09:45 - Marcus Li: Started shadow deployment in eu-west-1. Metrics dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ingest-normalization-shadow (private). Initial variance: median 0.8% — tracing into a set of mobile SDK events that lack request_id; plan to fallback to (customer_id + model_alias + payload_hash) for those cases.
notes: Trade-offs considered: immediate overwrite of historical aggregates simplifies UI but destroys audit trail; corrections maintain audit trail but add UI complexity.

If request_id is missing for a nontrivial fraction, we'll rely on a deterministic fingerprint that includes payload hash; this increases collision risk — mitigate by including event_type and timestamp_buckets.
Long-term: migrate streaming path to emit canonical_event_id at source to make dedupe both cheaper and more reliable. Schedule follow-up ENG ticket for instrumentation in SDKs.
